title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-19
notes:
West leads the ♣K against 4♥. South has 1 loser in spades, 1 loser in hearts, and 2 losers in clubs. If South loses a club trick at any point with the hope of ruffing a club in the dummy, the defense will counter by playing 2 rounds of hearts.

Since South can never score a club ruff in dummy, he should play to establish dummy's diamonds. Correct technique will allow South to almost always succeed as long as diamonds divide no worse than 4-2. South should win the first trick with the ♣A and cash dummy's top diamonds. A diamond is ruffed in the closed hand (it would not matter if West could overruff with the ♥A) and South exits in clubs.

The defense must win and play 2 rounds of trump to stop South from ruffing his remaining club in the dummy. South can win the second round of trump in the dummy and ruff another diamond. South draws the rest of the trump (in 2 rounds if necessary) and uses dummy's ♠A as an entry to the established diamond winner.
